title: Domain allowlist entry rejected before startup
symptoms: ports are not supported in domain entries
URL paths and queries are not supported in domain entries
conditions: AWF rejects a --allow-domains or network.allowDomains entry during validation, before Squid starts

Entries containing a port, URL path or query, user information, or a non-HTTP(S) scheme are rejected on current main; before #11952 some could instead produce a non-matching ACL and a 403 (affected release range unknown)
HTTP and HTTPS prefixes are recognized case-insensitively and a single trailing slash is accepted
rootCause: The supplied domain entry contains a scheme or URL component that cannot be represented as a Squid domain ACL. AWF rejects it during validation rather than starting with a non-matching rule.

probe.expect: Compare the rejected entry in the startup error with the allowlist configuration and available options; redact sensitive details before sharing. Squid logs are not expected for this pre-start failure.

action: Use a specific bare domain or valid wildcard (optionally prefixed by http:// or https://), without a port, path, query or user information. For URL path filtering use --allow-urls with --ssl-bump. For a trusted HTTP/HTTPS host service on a non-standard port, allowlist its host and use --enable-host-access with --allow-host-ports; host access exposes services on permitted ports, so enable it only when appropriate. Keep egress filtering enabled.
